text:
alex: heads up — we keep seeing slow pod pending times when the GPU nodepools need to scale. wondering if anyone has a recommended CA expander/flags combo for bursty training jobs? :thinking:
priya: are these long-lived pods or short ephemeral jobs?
alex: mostly short 10-30m training/benchmarks, a few longer hyperparam sweeps. they show up in waves from CI and ad-hoc runs.
jason: for that pattern we used --expander=least-waste with some custom binpacking annotations. avoids launching lots of small nodes that sit idle.
chen: +1 least-waste but you need to tune max-node-provision-time and scale-down-delay aggressively. default 10m provisioning can kill cold-starts for GPUs.
alex: what values worked?
jason: we set --max-node-provision-time=20m and --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m for GPU pools. also --scale-down-delay-after-add=5m so newly added capacity doesn't disappear while pods are still binding.
priya: watch out for PDBs — we had CA evict nodes during rolling updates. We added node annotations to prefer eviction from CPU pools first. also used nodeAffinity + topologySpread to keep critical services on non-gpu nodes.
marta: did you use balance-similar-node-group? we have mutliple instance types across regions and CA was thrashing between pools.
chen: yes, --balance-similar-node-groups=true helped, but only if the node groups are labeled consistently. otherwise the comparator treats them as different.
alex: we also see scale-to-zero problems: cold nodes take 8-12m to enter Ready for CUDA. Is there a way to pre-warm? :cry:
jason: you can pre-provision a tiny warm pool (1-2 nodes) with a toleration to keep them from being autoscaled away. cheap if you use spot but careful with eviction.
priya: alternatively set a short grace period on the CA for GPU pools and rely on burst credits — but that ups cost.
infra-bot: deploy-cadashboard: cluster-autoscaler metrics -> ProvisioningTime p95 = 9m, ScaleDowns in last 24h = 4
chen: infra-bot stats suggest p95 is borderline. I'd bump --max-node-provision-time to 25m and monitor p90/p99. also add --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false? depends if pods use local scratch.
alex: can someone draft a recommended flag set + a k8s Deploy manifest for a warm pool? I can run it in dev first.
marta: I'll post a small snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gpu-warm-pool
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: "true"
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "gpu-warm-pool"
        operator: "Exists"
      nodeSelector:
        node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: gpu-spot-small
      containers:
      - name: pause
        image: busybox
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 999999"]
```
priya: add a lifecycle hook to run a quick nvidia-smi once every 5m to keep CUDA JIT caches warm if you need sub-2m startup, same image as jobs use.
jason: also consider --expander=random for cases where CA can't guess right. it spreads risk but can raise cost. use it only as fallback.
chen: last thing: enable CA's scale down candidates logging and set --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false so system-attributed pods don't confuse scale decisions.
alex: solid. I'll test with least-waste + max-node-provision-time=25m, scale-down-unneeded=15m, delay-after-add=5m, balance-similar=true, and add the warm-pool deployment. will report results tomorrow. :rocket:
marta: cheers — if you post numbers I can help tune the binpacker config for least-waste.
alex: thanks all, assigning follow-up to myself.
